svg.title: Recommended production architecture: a private file share tied to Microsoft Entra ID
svg.text: Recommended production design: a private file share tied to Microsoft Entra ID
This design is a recommendation and is not deployed yet. It removes the shared password and every public address from the proof of concept.

g.text: Run the AWS VPN Client app.
Signs VPN users in with SAML.
domain that stays in sync with
Entra ID. The gateway joins it.
AWS Region closest to the users
Office laptops reach the gateway over AWS Site-to-Site VPN or AWS Direct
Connect. Users sign in to the share with their own domain accounts.
Remote users connect the AWS VPN Client and sign in with Microsoft Entra ID.
The file-sharing port is never reachable from the internet.
The gateway serves files from a cache disk sized for a month of work, so
most file opens never wait for Amazon S3.
The gateway reaches AWS services through VPC endpoints, so the subnet
needs no internet gateway and no public IP address.
Saved files are uploaded to the bucket, which is encrypted with a customer
managed AWS KMS key and keeps old versions.
AWS Data Exports writes new CUR files into the bucket every day, and they
appear on the share within 5 minutes.
The gateway joins the Microsoft Entra Domain Services domain over a
site-to-site VPN to Azure, so folder permissions use Entra groups.
Amazon CloudWatch collects the gateway's health logs and raises alarms. Icons come from the AWS Architecture Icons package released on 31 July 2026.
